**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §3.1. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

To compare two orders we need a magnitude measure. A norm must be nonnegative, homogeneous and obey the triangle inequality. Different norms encode different notions of operational cost.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
\|\boldsymbol x\|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i x_i^2},\qquad \|\boldsymbol x\|_1=\sum_i|x_i|
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

For x=(3,4), the Euclidean norm equals 5 while its L1 norm equals 7. The values are not contradictory: they use different geometry and emphasise different trade-offs.

## What follows, and what does not

A scale issue appears when distance is measured in kilometres but price in cents. Standardisation or a carefully chosen metric may be necessary before comparing features.

## Test your reasoning

For x=(1,-2), compute the L1 and L2 norms and check that both are nonnegative.
